answer_text:
Let
\[
f_n(x)=\frac{x^{-2}}{\sqrt[n]{1+x^{3n}}},\qquad x\ge 1.
\]

First find the pointwise limit. For \(x\ge 1\),
\[
\sqrt[n]{1+x^{3n}}
= x^3\left(1+x^{-3n}\right)^{1/n},
\]
so
\[
f_n(x)=x^{-5}\left(1+x^{-3n}\right)^{-1/n}.
\]
For \(x>1\), \(x^{-3n}\to 0\), hence \((1+x^{-3n})^{-1/n}\to 1\). For \(x=1\), \((1+1)^{-1/n}=2^{-1/n}\to 1\). Therefore
\[
f_n(x)\to x^{-5}\qquad\text{for all }x\ge 1.
\]

Now dominate \(f_n\). Since \(x\ge 1\),
\[
1+x^{3n}\ge x^{3n},
\]
so
\[
\sqrt[n]{1+x^{3n}}\ge x^3.
\]
Thus
\[
0\le f_n(x)\le \frac{x^{-2}}{x^3}=x^{-5}.
\]
The dominating function is integrable on \([1,\infty)\):
\[
\int_1^\infty x^{-5}\,dx
=
\left[-\frac{1}{4x^4}\right]_1^\infty
=
\frac14.
\]

By the Dominated Convergence Theorem,
\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}\int_{[1,\infty[}
\frac{x^{-2}}{\sqrt[n]{1+x^{3n}}}\,d\lambda
=
\int_1^\infty x^{-5}\,dx
=
\frac14.
\]

Hence the limit converges and equals
\[
\boxed{\frac14}
\]
